title: Tomato Early Blight, Leaf Curl Virus and Weather-Linked Spraying Rules
region: Maharashtra (Pune, Nashik, Satara), Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) & IMD Agromet Division Pune
summary: Management of Early Blight (Alternaria solani) and Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV) with critical weather rules for chemical applications.
content: Symptoms: 1) Early Blight: Dark brown to black circular spots with concentric rings ('target-board' appearance) on lower leaves first, spreading upwards. Heavy during warm humid weather (temperatures 24-29°C with intermittent drizzle). 2) Tomato Leaf Curl: Leaves curl upwards and inwards, become puckered, leathery, and yellowed with severe stunting of shoots and dropping of flowers. Transmitted by Whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci). Weather Rules for Spraying: A) Wind speed > 15 km/h: Postpone spraying to prevent droplet drift away from crop target. B) Rain forecast within 3 hours: Do NOT spray fungicides or systemic insecticides without sticker/spreader; product will wash off. C) High temperature (>35°C at midday): Avoid spraying EC (emulsifiable concentrate) formulations to prevent phytotoxicity/leaf scorching; spray in early morning (7-10 AM) or late afternoon (4-6 PM). Disease Management: Rogue out leaf curl affected plants at early stage. Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L for Early Blight prevention. For curative control of blight, spray Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1 ml/L. For whitefly control: Install yellow sticky traps (25/acre) and spray Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2 g/L.
